name: Pass-the-Hash with smbclient
description: Use an NTLM hash directly to authenticate to SMB shares with smbclient — no password cracking required. The --pw-nt-hash flag tells smbclient to treat the supplied string as an NT hash rather than a plaintext password.
notes: smbclient with --pw-nt-hash uses the NT portion of the NTLM hash. Domain can be a workgroup name for local accounts (use the hostname or WORKGROUP). Combine with -c for non-interactive file operations. impacket-smbclient and impacket-psexec are alternatives when you need code execution vs. just file access. Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 15 (Password Attacks).

variations.caption: Connect to ADMIN$ share as local Administrator
variations.label: smbclient \\\\<target>\\ADMIN$ -U …

variations.caption: Upload a file to the share
variations.label: smbclient (hash) - upload

variations.caption: PTH with impacket-psexec for code execution (SYSTEM shell)
variations.label: impacket-psexec

variations.caption: PTH with WMI execution (less noisy than psexec)
variations.label: impacket-wmiexec

variations.caption: CrackMapExec PTH: enumerate all accessible shares
variations.label: cme (hash) - enum shares

variations.caption: CrackMapExec PTH: spray hash across subnet and run command
variations.label: cme (hash) - exec on CIDR

examples.caption: PEN-200 Ch15: access SMB share with harvested Administrator hash

recommended.note: Dump hashes with mimikatz lsadump::sam or sekurlsa::logonpasswords
Obtain domain account hashes via DCSync
PTH with mimikatz sekurlsa::pth to spawn a process on Windows

defense.why_it_works: NTLM authentication uses a challenge-response mechanism where the client proves knowledge of the password by applying it to a server challenge. The actual plaintext password is never transmitted — only the NTLM hash is used in the computation. smbclient -U 'domain/user%' --pw-nt-hash accepts the NTLM hash directly in place of the password, authenticating as the user without cracking the hash.
defense.prerequisites: NTLM hash of the target account (from LSASS dump, DCSync, SAM dump). smbclient on Linux attacker. SMB port 445 accessible. SMB signing disabled on target (or NTLMv2 accepted).
defense.impact: T1550.002 Use Alternate Authentication Material: Pass the Hash. Lateral movement to any SMB-accessible resource where the hash is valid. Applicable to any Windows host where the account is a local admin or has SMB access. Works against all Windows versions when NTLM authentication is allowed.
defense.detection:
Event 4624 type 3 (network logon) with NTLM authentication from unexpected source IP. Event 4625: failed PtH attempt. Sysmon Event 3: SMB connection from Linux/non-Windows host (no typical Windows source info). MDI: 'Pass-the-Hash' detection. NTLM audit logs: Event 4776 on DC for NTLMv1/v2 success.
Stolen Kerberos tickets or token impersonation: logon sessions from accounts without expected interactive logon events (DET0338/AN0954).
Access tokens or SSH keys used without corresponding login shell or PAM module activity, especially for remote execution (AN0955).
Token replay or impersonation in federated logins without interactive browser session or MFA prompts (AN0956).
OAuth token reuse from different geographic regions without full login events (AN0957).
Container process using mounted cloud credentials or token cache without known orchestration (AN0958).
Access token reuse for SharePoint or Outlook APIs without interactive user context (AN0959).
Instance metadata token use across instances or misuse of short-lived tokens for different roles (AN0960).
defense.artifacts: Event 4624 type 3 with NTLM auth from unexpected IP | MDI: PtH alert | Event 4776 on DC for NTLM validation | Netflow: SMB connection from Linux/attacker IP | Event 4625 for failed PtH attempts
defense.prevention:
Enable SMB signing (blocks relay; doesn't block PtH directly). LAPS for unique local admin passwords (PtH with local admin only works on that one host). Enable Credential Guard (prevents NTLM hash extraction from LSASS). Protected Users group (no NTLM auth for members). Restrict NTLM authentication (NTLMv1 disabled; NTLMv2 required). MDI deployment.
Account Use Policies: Restrict authentication material use outside expected contexts.
Active Directory Configuration: Configure AD to prevent certain techniques; use SID Filtering.
Application Developer Guidance: Implement token binding (Azure AD token protection, OAuth DPoP/Proof of Possession) to cryptographically bind tokens.
Audit: Scan for insecure configurations and potential weaknesses.
Password Policies: Set and enforce secure password policies.
Privileged Account Management: Limit credential overlap across systems to reduce lateral movement risk.
User Account Management: Enforce least privilege; prevent domain users from being local admins on multiple systems.
defense.evasion: PtH with domain accounts works across all SMB hosts where the domain account is an admin. Use impacket tools for stealthier PtH (psexec.py, wmiexec.py). Combine with Overpass-the-Hash to convert NTLM hash to Kerberos ticket (avoids NTLM-specific detection).
defense.misconfiguration: Same local admin password on all workstations (no LAPS). NTLM not restricted. Credential Guard not deployed. MDI not deployed. SMB signing not required.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Same local admin hash on all workstations (no LAPS):
# Mimikatz dumps: Administrator:aad3b435b51404eeaad3b435b51404ee:8846f7eaee8fb117ad06bdd830b7586c
# smbclient -U 'CORP/Administrator%' //ws02/C$ --pw-nt-hash 8846f7eaee8fb117ad06bdd830b7586c
# → Access to ALL workstations via one hash

# NTLM not restricted:
(Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa').LmCompatibilityLevel  # 3 or lower allows NTLMv1
defense.secure_config:
# LAPS: unique local admin passwords per host:
# Install LAPS → extend AD schema → GPO:
# Computer Config → Admin Templates → LAPS → Password Settings: Enabled
# Length: 25, Complexity: All characters, Age: 30 days

# Disable NTLMv1:
Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa' -Name LmCompatibilityLevel -Value 5
# 5 = NTLMv2 only on client; DCs refuse anything below NTLMv2

# Restrict NTLM to specific servers:
# Computer Config → Windows Settings → Security Settings → Local Policies → Security Options
# → Network security: Restrict NTLM: Outgoing NTLM traffic to remote servers: Deny all

# Protected Users (no NTLM for members):
Add-ADGroupMember 'Protected Users' 'DomainAdmin1'
